Dominance Enforcement.def: Maintaining a position of power over another person by controlling their choices and morally condemning any resistance to that control; dominance is held in place by two moves at once -- tightening control, and treating noncompliance as a character flaw rather than a disagreement.
Dominance Enforcement.body: This complex pairs Controller's drive to manage outcomes and other people's behavior with Judge's drive to find people wanting and say so. Where either saboteur alone might produce rigidity or criticism, together they produce an enforced hierarchy: control backed by moral condemnation of whoever will not comply. This is a research-informed expansion of the owner-ruled name and saboteur pairing above, not a clinical diagnosis.
Dominance Enforcement.inferenceBasis: The complex name, glyph and saboteur pairing are explicitly owner-ruled in canon.json (tag R). The behavioral template, trigger mechanism, lived example, impact and practice below are a research-informed expansion built from two separately validated literatures (assertions of dominance within the PID-5 Antagonism domain, and contempt as a moral emotion), not from a study of 'Dominance Enforcement' as a named construct, because no such named construct exists in the literature I could find.
Dominance Enforcement.behavior: May tightly manage another person's decisions, schedule, or environment and treat deviation from the plan as a problem to be corrected rather than a choice to be respected. When someone does not comply, the response is not limited to correction -- it carries visible disgust, disapproval or moral framing ('that was wrong of you,' not just 'that didn't work'), so resistance is answered with both control and condemnation.
Dominance Enforcement.triggerMechanism: A loss of predictability, disobedience, or being told no can activate the controlling response. A perceived moral lapse, disrespect, or violation of an unstated standard can separately activate the contemptuous-judgment response. In this complex the two fire together: the same incident reads as both a control problem and a character problem.
Dominance Enforcement.livedExample: A person sets a household or team rule unilaterally. When someone deviates from it, the response is not 'let's talk about why that happened' but a tightening of oversight paired with a remark that frames the deviation as evidence of the other person's laziness, selfishness or bad character, and the rule is then enforced more strictly going forward.
Dominance Enforcement.impact: Erodes trust and psychological safety. People comply to avoid moral judgment rather than because they agree, so apparent cooperation can mask resentment or withdrawal. Feedback becomes one-directional, and the relationship organizes around supervision rather than mutual agreement.
Dominance Enforcement.practice: Before tightening control, name the actual need for predictability out loud and ask whether it requires controlling the other person's choice or only communicating the stakes. Before passing judgment, separate the behavior from the person's character, and check whether the same standard would be applied to yourself in the same situation. Make room for the other person's account before concluding noncompliance was a moral failing.
Dominance Enforcement.oppositeDefinition: Collaborative authority: holding structure, standards and accountability through invitation, transparency and respect for another person's agency, without requiring control over their choices or treating disagreement as a moral failing.

Blame Displacement.def: Converting one's own anger, failure or shame into an accusation against someone else, so responsibility for an outcome relocates onto another person rather than staying with the one who produced it.
Blame Displacement.body: Aggressor supplies the charge -- anger, often disproportionate to the triggering event -- and Deflector supplies the redirection, moving responsibility for that charge off the self and onto someone else before it can be examined. Together they produce a pattern where conflict reliably resolves with someone else at fault, regardless of what actually happened.
Blame Displacement.inferenceBasis: The name and saboteur pairing are owner-ruled (canon.json tag R). The behavioral content below draws on real, replicated findings about hostile attribution and blame externalization under threat; it is this project's synthesis of that literature onto the named saboteur pair, not a direct study of 'Blame Displacement' as a construct.
Blame Displacement.behavior: May respond to a mistake, conflict or criticism by immediately asserting that it happened because of someone else's action, hostility or incompetence, before any investigation of the actual sequence of events. Acknowledging one's own contribution tends to come late, if at all, and often only after the blame attribution has already been stated to others.
Blame Displacement.triggerMechanism: A threat to self-image -- being caught in an error, criticized, or confronted with a bad outcome one contributed to -- can activate a rapid, pre-reflective attribution of hostile intent or fault onto another party. This is closer to an automatic interpretive bias than a deliberate lie in the moment it happens, even though the effect on the other person is the same.
Blame Displacement.livedExample: A shared task goes wrong. Before the sequence of events has been established, the person states that it happened because a colleague dropped the ball or was careless, and continues to hold that account even once facts emerge that complicate it.
Blame Displacement.impact: Prevents repair, because the party actually responsible is never named by the person who caused the harm. The other person accumulates blame that is not theirs, trust erodes, and the underlying problem (whatever actually caused the failure) goes uncorrected because it was never accurately identified.
Blame Displacement.practice: Before assigning cause, separate the observable sequence of events from the felt sense of threat or shame in the moment. State what is actually known to have happened before stating who is at fault. Name your own contribution first, even if partial, before describing anyone else's.
Blame Displacement.oppositeDefinition: Accountable attribution: examining what actually happened before assigning cause, naming one's own contribution without being prompted, and tolerating the discomfort of fault landing on oneself when it belongs there.

Superiority-Persecution.def: Holding two positions on others at once: moral or competitive superiority, and a persistent felt sense of being unfairly targeted by the very people one considers beneath oneself. The two do not alternate -- they co-occur, which is what the shell's own note ('Victim runs split') is naming.
Superiority-Persecution.body: Hyper-Achiever supplies a standing claim to being better -- more capable, more deserving, more hardworking than others -- while Victim, rather than running as ordinary felt helplessness, runs here as a claim of persecution: being undervalued, misunderstood or attacked by the people the superiority claim places below oneself. The combination is self-sealing: criticism confirms persecution, and persecution confirms that one is, after all, superior to whoever is doing the persecuting.
Superiority-Persecution.inferenceBasis: The name, saboteur pairing and the 'Victim runs split' note are owner-ruled (canon.json tag R). The behavioral template below is grounded in a named, validated personality-psychology construct (Tendency for Interpersonal Victimhood) that independently measures moral superiority, need for recognition and low empathy for others' comparable claims together; mapping that construct onto this specific saboteur pair is this project's synthesis.
Superiority-Persecution.behavior: May claim moral or competitive high ground while simultaneously describing oneself as misunderstood, undervalued or unfairly treated by others, often in the same conversation. Shows a high need for recognition of one's own effort or suffering, rumination on specific instances of being wronged, and comparatively little recognition that others might have equally valid claims to being wronged.
Superiority-Persecution.triggerMechanism: Being overlooked, criticized, or not sufficiently credited for one's effort or achievement can activate both halves of the pattern at once: the superiority claim ('I am clearly the one who worked hardest/did this right') and the persecution claim ('and they are the ones treating me unfairly for it').
Superiority-Persecution.livedExample: A person who put in the most visible effort on a shared project is not singled out for thanks. They experience this as proof both that they are better than the team and that the team is treating them unjustly, and become preoccupied with the omission rather than the project's outcome.
Superiority-Persecution.impact: Makes ordinary feedback and disagreement difficult to receive, because disagreement is read as persecution rather than as information. Relationships around the person can come to organize around managing the sense of being wronged, and the person's own view of others' comparable claims to unfair treatment tends to be dismissed.
Superiority-Persecution.practice: Name the specific unmet need (recognition, credit, acknowledgment) separately from a global claim of being persecuted. Check whether the same standard for 'unfair treatment' would be applied if someone else made the identical claim. Invite an outside perspective before concluding the situation was persecution rather than an ordinary oversight.
Superiority-Persecution.oppositeDefinition: Grounded standing: recognizing one's own effort and contribution without needing to rank it above others', and distinguishing an actual injustice from an ordinary oversight or disagreement, without defaulting to a persecution narrative.

Narcissistic.fam: Narcissism (owner-dictated four-part structure: entitlement, justification, comparison, judgment; three of four parts currently addressed by saboteurs)
Narcissistic.def: Interpreting situations through entitlement, self-justification, competitive comparison and moral judgment of others, in service of a self-image that must be maintained as superior. The structural (saboteur-built) form of grandiose narcissism, distinct from, but describing the same territory as, the existing higher-order Narcissism record.
Narcissistic.body: Controller supplies the drive to manage outcomes and other people so the superior self-image is not disturbed. Hyper-Achiever supplies the comparison -- measuring the self against others and needing to come out ahead. Judge supplies the moral condemnation of anyone who falls short of the standard the person holds for others but not for themselves. The owner's own four-part framing (entitlement, justification, comparison, judgment) names one more element, entitlement-as-justification, that does not yet have its own saboteur address in canon.json; this record does not attempt to supply one.
Narcissistic.inferenceBasis: The name, saboteur pairing and the owner's four-part framing are explicitly owner-ruled (canon.json tag R, 'Lance dictated'). The behavioral template below reuses the same real external literature as the project's existing DESCENT Narcissism record, because this is the same real construct described at a different schema tier, not a new territory requiring new sources.
Narcissistic.behavior: May expect special treatment without having to ask for it (entitlement), explain or reframe one's own actions after the fact rather than accounting for them directly (justification), measure one's standing against others on an ongoing basis (comparison), and hold others to standards not applied to oneself (judgment). Vulnerable shame can sit underneath the presentation; it can vary by context and by which saboteur is most active at a given moment.
Narcissistic.triggerMechanism: A status threat, being asked to account for one's own behavior, being outperformed, or being treated as ordinary rather than exceptional can activate a defensive move through whichever of the three addressed saboteurs is most available -- tightening control, re-justifying the action, or judging the other party -- to restore the superior self-image.
Narcissistic.livedExample: Asked to explain a decision that hurt someone, the person offers a justification that reframes the decision as necessary or as the other party's fault, mentions their own track record as evidence of good judgment, and criticizes the other party's conduct in the same breath.
Narcissistic.impact: Reduces mutuality, trust and the capacity to repair harm, because the other person's account is treated as secondary to protecting the self-image, and accountability conversations tend to end in comparison or judgment rather than resolution.
Narcissistic.practice: Before justifying, state the plain facts of what happened. Before comparing, ask whether the comparison serves the other person or only one's own self-image. Before judging, apply the same standard to yourself that is being applied to the other person.
Narcissistic.oppositeDefinition: Grounded self-worth with humility, reciprocal empathy, accountability, and respect for others as equally real -- the same working counterpart the existing DESCENT Narcissism record already names as 'Grounded Self-Worth,' here applied to the three-saboteur structural form.

Machiavellian Tactics.fam: Machiavellianism (tactical layer; Rebel saboteur removed from this complex and reclassified as a Jungian archetype elsewhere in canon)
Machiavellian Tactics.def: The tactical layer of the Machiavellian pattern: a standing assumption that other people are also acting out of self-interest (Skeptic), used to justify deliberately managing what they see and know in order to control an outcome (Manipulator). A narrower slice than the full Machiavellian trait structure -- the tactics, not the whole stack.
Machiavellian Tactics.body: Skeptic supplies the cynical premise -- other people's stated motives are not fully trusted -- and Manipulator supplies the response: selective disclosure, impression management, or deception, framed internally as reasonable self-protection against people who are assumed to be doing the same thing. Unlike the existing DESCENT Machiavellianism hyper-complex, which is the full narcissism-plus-suppressed-empathy stack, this complex is the two-saboteur tactical core underneath it.
Machiavellian Tactics.inferenceBasis: The name, saboteur pairing and the Rebel-removal note are owner-ruled (canon.json tag R). The behavioral template below draws on the foundational, well-replicated Machiavellianism trait literature; narrowing that trait down to a two-saboteur 'tactics' slice is this project's own structural choice and has not itself been separately validated as a sub-construct.
Machiavellian Tactics.behavior: May use selective disclosure, strategic impression management, or outright deception to secure a desired outcome, while privately assuming the other party would do the same if given the chance. Tends to present the tactic, internally, as necessary caution rather than manipulation.
Machiavellian Tactics.triggerMechanism: A competitive situation, a desired outcome that depends on another person's choice, or a perceived risk of being deceived first can activate the shift from open negotiation toward controlling what information the other party has access to.
Machiavellian Tactics.livedExample: In a negotiation, the person assumes the other party is already angling for advantage, and pre-emptively withholds or frames information to secure a better outcome, experiencing this as self-defense rather than as a tactic being used against someone who has not yet done anything untrustworthy.
Machiavellian Tactics.impact: Undermines informed consent and durable trust. Even when the tactic succeeds in the moment, relationships built this way tend to become transactional, and once the pattern is noticed by others, they withdraw good faith pre-emptively -- which then appears to confirm the original cynical premise.
Machiavellian Tactics.practice: Name the actual goal and what is genuinely at stake, out loud, before deciding how much information to share. Test the assumption that the other party is acting in bad faith against actual evidence rather than acting on the assumption by default. Offer the other party real information and a genuine option to decline.
Machiavellian Tactics.oppositeDefinition: Transparent dealing: making the goal and relevant information explicit, testing cynical assumptions against evidence rather than acting on them pre-emptively, and giving others a genuine, informed choice -- the same direction the existing DESCENT Machiavellianism record's counterpart names at the full-stack level, applied here to the tactical layer.

Antisocial.fam: Antisocial / psychopathy spectrum (Rebel saboteur removed from this complex)
Antisocial.def: Disregard for other people's rights or safety, combined with deflecting responsibility for the resulting harm onto circumstances or other people, so accountability does not land even when the harm is direct and observable.
Antisocial.body: Aggressor supplies disregard for others' rights or safety in pursuit of one's own aims -- action taken without meaningful consideration of who it affects -- and Deflector supplies the follow-on move: when confronted, responsibility for the harm is relocated elsewhere rather than acknowledged. This is a more severe and more global pattern than Blame Displacement (Complex 2), which shares the same two saboteurs but is framed at the narrower level of shifting blame in a specific conflict rather than a standing disregard for others' rights.
Antisocial.inferenceBasis: The name and saboteur pairing are owner-ruled (canon.json tag R). The behavioral template below draws on DSM-5 antisocial personality disorder criteria and the triarchic model of psychopathy (meanness and disinhibition facets); a two-saboteur pairing is a thin structural basis for a pattern this clinically significant, which is reflected in the confidence score below, not in the behavioral claims themselves.
Antisocial.behavior: May act in ways that disregard other people's rights, safety or wellbeing, with limited forward planning for the consequences to others. When confronted with the resulting harm, responsibility is reliably relocated -- onto circumstances, onto the other person's own actions, or onto bad luck -- rather than acknowledged, and there is little visible change in future behavior as a result of the confrontation.
Antisocial.triggerMechanism: An opportunity for personal gain, a boundary that frustrates an immediate goal, or being held accountable for a consequence can activate action with limited regard for who is affected, followed by deflection of responsibility once the harm becomes visible to others.
Antisocial.livedExample: Harm to another person results directly from the person's own action. When confronted, the explanation offered relocates the cause to something or someone else, and the same kind of action recurs afterward without a visible change in behavior.
Antisocial.impact: Creates real risk to the safety, finances or wellbeing of people around the person. Ordinary accountability conversations tend not to work, because responsibility does not land on the person who caused the harm; relationships and systems around the person may need documented boundaries and outside oversight rather than relying on remorse or insight appearing on its own.
Antisocial.practice: Do not rely on an expectation that remorse will appear spontaneously. Require concrete, observed behavior change rather than an account or apology alone. Use documentation and outside accountability structures where real harm or risk is present, and involve a qualified professional when safety or functioning is significantly affected.
Antisocial.oppositeDefinition: Accountable regard: taking other people's rights and safety into account before acting, and accepting responsibility for resulting harm without relocating it onto circumstances or other people.

Oscillation.fam: Clinical filing, internal only: Bipolar (canon.json's own R-tagged note, 'Filed as Bipolar in the March table'; per SNIFFER_SPEC.md section 5's HARD GUARD and engine.js's CODE_ALIAS table, this filing is translation-only and must never be presented as a diagnosis)
Oscillation.def: Moving between an activated, outwardly expressive high state and a flat, aggrieved low state without settling at a stable baseline in between -- the complex names the movement itself, not either pole alone.
Oscillation.body: Dramatizer supplies amplified, theatrical emotional expression and rapid shifts in presented affect. Restless supplies elevated energy and a pull toward activity that resists sitting still. Victim supplies the low pole: sadness, resentment, and a felt sense of being acted upon rather than acting. Together the three move the person between an energized, attention-seeking high and a flat, hard-done-by low, structurally analogous to -- but not clinically equivalent to -- a mood-episode cycle.
Oscillation.inferenceBasis: The name, saboteur triad and clinical filing are owner-ruled (canon.json tag R). Cross-checked against engine.js's CODE_ALIAS table (code X07), which independently corroborates the same three-saboteur assignment via an internal manuscript I have not read today (see flag above). The behavioral content below is this pilot batch's research expansion using real external literature on bipolar-spectrum mood structure; it is not a claim that 'Oscillation' is itself a validated external construct, and it must not be read as diagnosing bipolar disorder in anyone.
Oscillation.behavior: May shift between seeking attention through dramatized, high-energy expression and pressured activity, and a flat state marked by sadness and a sense of grievance -- feeling that circumstances or other people, not one's own choices, produced the low. The shift is not always visible to others as sudden, even when it is not steady from the inside.
Oscillation.triggerMechanism: Possible activating factors include disrupted sleep or routine, unmet needs for recognition during the high phase, and accumulated setbacks or invalidation feeding the low phase. This is a working hypothesis about the saboteur pattern, not a claim about the biological or circadian mechanisms of a mood disorder, which are multifactorial and not settled by this record.
Oscillation.livedExample: A person is the most animated, visible presence in a group for a stretch of days, initiating plans and drawing attention to their own excitement. Within the same week, the energy drops, plans are abandoned, and the same person describes feeling let down by everyone who 'didn't show up' for the plans they themselves generated.
Oscillation.impact: Makes the person's support, energy and attention unpredictable for people around them, and can leave both the person and others unsure which state is the 'real' one. Can exhaust relationships that reorganize around managing the swing rather than addressing either state directly.
Oscillation.practice: Track the pattern itself, not just the current pole: note what preceded a shift into either the high or the low. Build in rest and routine before a high state burns out into a low one. Separate the grievance narrative of the low state from an accurate account of what others actually did or didn't do. Seek a qualified clinical evaluation if the swings are severe, persistent, or risk safety -- this record is not a substitute for that assessment.
Oscillation.oppositeDefinition: Stable affective range: holding a workable mood baseline through both setbacks and successes, expressing enthusiasm and disappointment without the pattern resolving into an attention-seeking high or an aggrieved low.

Abandonment Reactivity.fam: Clinical filing, internal only: Borderline Personality Disorder (canon.json's own R-tagged note, 'Filed as BPD'; translation-only per the same HARD GUARD and CODE_ALIAS convention noted under Oscillation above)
Abandonment Reactivity.def: A standing sensitivity to real or anticipated abandonment that organizes behavior around preventing it -- through appeasement, through a self-image that shifts to match what the relationship seems to require, and through a felt sense of being wronged when connection feels threatened.
Abandonment Reactivity.body: Victim supplies the affective core: sadness and resentment that surface when connection feels at risk, and a sense of being done to rather than choosing. People-Pleaser supplies the preventive strategy: adjusting behavior, withholding disagreement, and seeking approval to keep the other person close. Imposter supplies an unstable sense of self that shifts depending on who the person is trying to keep -- less a fixed identity than a fit to whatever the relationship currently seems to need. Together they describe a pattern organized around the threat of loss rather than around any one fixed trait.
Abandonment Reactivity.inferenceBasis: The name, saboteur triad and clinical filing are owner-ruled (canon.json tag R). The behavioral template below draws on two separately real, well-established bodies of work: the DSM-5 BPD criteria themselves (abandonment fear, identity disturbance, chronic emptiness) and Linehan's biosocial model of BPD. Mapping Victim/People-Pleaser/Imposter onto those three specific DSM-5 criteria is this project's own structural choice, not an independently validated three-way split in the literature.
Abandonment Reactivity.behavior: May read ordinary distance, disagreement, or a partner's independent plans as a sign of impending loss, and respond by increasing appeasement, suppressing one's own preferences, or presenting a version of self calibrated to what seems most likely to keep the relationship intact. The resulting self-presentation can feel, from the inside, less like a stable identity and more like a performance tuned to the audience.
Abandonment Reactivity.triggerMechanism: A partner's unavailability, a perceived slight, an upcoming separation, or any cue read as a precursor to loss can activate appeasement and self-adjustment at once. Linehan's biosocial model frames the underlying vulnerability as heightened emotional sensitivity meeting an environment that did not reliably validate the person's internal experience; I'm naming that model as real background, not asserting it explains any individual case, and empirical support for its specific interaction term is mixed (see sourcing notes).
Abandonment Reactivity.livedExample: A partner makes plans without first checking in. Before anything is said, the person begins reviewing what they might have done wrong, agrees to whatever the partner wants in the next interaction regardless of their own preference, and afterward cannot clearly describe what they themselves had wanted that day.
Abandonment Reactivity.impact: Can make the person's stated preferences unreliable information for people close to them, since those preferences shift under abandonment pressure. Relationships can become organized around reassurance-seeking, and the person's own sense of who they are outside a given relationship can stay thin or inconsistent.
Abandonment Reactivity.practice: Name the fear of loss explicitly rather than acting on it indirectly through appeasement. Before adjusting behavior to fit a relationship, check what you actually want, independent of what you believe the other person needs. Build a sense of self that holds steady across relationships rather than one that is reconstituted inside each one. Seek a qualified clinician for a full evaluation and for dialectical behavior therapy or comparable support if the pattern is severe -- this record describes a working pattern, not a treatment plan.
Abandonment Reactivity.oppositeDefinition: Secure relatedness: tolerating ordinary distance and disagreement without reading them as abandonment, holding a stable sense of self across relationships, and expressing one's own preferences even under relational uncertainty.

Rigidity.fam: Clinical filing, internal only: Obsessive-Compulsive Personality Disorder (canon.json's own R-tagged note, 'Filed as OCPD'; translation-only per the HARD GUARD and CODE_ALIAS convention noted under Oscillation above). NOTE: this name is also live, independently, as a hypercomplex-tier framework mode (Cluster IV, 'independently derived' per SNIFFER_SPEC.md section 5) -- see flag above.
Rigidity.def: A preoccupation with rules, order, and getting things exactly right, paired with a standing watchfulness for error or disorder, that together crowd out flexibility even when flexibility would serve the actual goal better.
Rigidity.body: Stickler supplies devotion to rules, details, and one correct way of doing things. Perfectionist supplies the specific drive toward flawless execution that can stall completion rather than support it. Hyper-Vigilant supplies ongoing scanning for error, disorder, or deviation from the standard. Together they produce a pattern where control and correctness are held above adaptability, efficiency, or other people's needs, even when the situation has already changed.
Rigidity.inferenceBasis: The name, saboteur triad and clinical filing are owner-ruled (canon.json tag R). The behavioral template below draws on the real, peer-reviewed OCPD literature, mapped onto this specific three-saboteur triad as this project's own structural choice. This record does not resolve, and should not be read as having resolved, the naming collision with the existing hypercomplex:Rigidity record flagged above.
Rigidity.behavior: May insist on one correct method even after it stops fitting the situation, delay or fail to complete tasks because they do not yet meet a self-set standard, and notice and flag deviations, disorder or rule-breaking in the environment or in other people's work well before anyone else does. Devotion to work and detail can come at the expense of leisure, relationships, or the actual deadline.
Rigidity.triggerMechanism: Uncertainty, perceived disorder, an error (one's own or someone else's), or a threat to a known, controllable method can activate tightened adherence to rules and heightened scanning for what else might be wrong. These are hypotheses to test against observed behavior, not assumed causes.
Rigidity.livedExample: A process that used to work no longer fits a changed situation. Rather than adapting the method, the person insists on following it exactly as before, becomes visibly uneasy at suggestions to deviate, and spends disproportionate time checking the work for errors that would not materially affect the outcome.
Rigidity.impact: Can impair collaboration, timeliness and adaptation to new information, since the method and the standard are prioritized over the actual goal. Co-workers or family members can experience ongoing correction and little tolerance for alternative approaches, even workable ones.
Rigidity.practice: Name the purpose behind the rule or standard before defending it. Ask what has actually changed in the situation. Generate at least one workable alternative before rejecting it. Separate 'this does not meet my standard' from 'this will not work' -- they are not the same claim, and only one of them is about the actual outcome.
Rigidity.oppositeDefinition: Flexible integrity: preserving real standards and follow-through while adapting method to context, tolerating imperfection that does not affect the actual outcome, and treating a changed situation as a reason to update rather than a threat to resist.

Attention Seeking.fam: Clinical filing, internal only: Histrionic Personality Disorder (canon.json's own R-tagged note, 'Filed as Histrionic'; translation-only per the HARD GUARD and CODE_ALIAS convention noted under Oscillation above)
Attention Seeking.def: A standing need to be the focus of attention, pursued through dramatized emotional display, through shaping oneself to be liked, and through a self-presentation that leans on impression and feeling rather than verifiable detail.
Attention Seeking.body: Dramatizer supplies theatrical, exaggerated emotional expression aimed at drawing and holding notice. People-Pleaser supplies the drive to be liked and approved of, which channels the display toward whatever earns warmth from the audience in the moment. Dreamer supplies an impressionistic, feeling-forward self-presentation -- light on specific detail, oriented toward how a story lands rather than its exact accuracy. Together they produce a pattern organized around being noticed and liked rather than around any specific content being communicated.
Attention Seeking.inferenceBasis: The name, saboteur triad and clinical filing are owner-ruled (canon.json tag R). The behavioral template below draws on the real DSM-5 HPD criteria, which is itself a comparatively thin and contested empirical category (see sourcing notes -- this is not a case of borrowing a rock-solid literature, and the confidence score reflects that honestly). Mapping Dramatizer/People-Pleaser/Dreamer onto specific HPD criteria is this project's own structural choice.
Attention Seeking.behavior: May become visibly uncomfortable or seek to redirect attention back to self when not the center of focus, present emotion in a dramatic or exaggerated register, shift presentation readily based on what seems to please the audience, and describe experiences in impressionistic, feeling-centered terms that are light on verifiable specifics.
Attention Seeking.triggerMechanism: Being overlooked, a conversation or situation moving its focus elsewhere, or a flat response to an emotional display can activate an escalation of expressiveness or a shift in self-presentation aimed at recovering attention and approval.
Attention Seeking.livedExample: In a group conversation, focus moves to someone else's news. The person re-centers the conversation on their own related, more dramatically told experience, delivered with more emotional color than specific detail, and visibly brightens once attention returns.
Attention Seeking.impact: Can make it hard for others to get a stable, detailed read on the person's actual experience, since the presentation is tuned to effect rather than accuracy. Attention and approval can start to function as the measure of whether an interaction went well, independent of its actual content.
Attention Seeking.practice: Before describing an experience, separate what actually happened from how you want it to land. Practice tolerating a conversation that is not centered on you without redirecting it. Notice when self-presentation is shifting to match what you believe the audience wants, and check that shift against what you actually think or feel.
Attention Seeking.oppositeDefinition: Grounded self-expression: sharing experience accurately and with genuine feeling, without needing to be the center of attention to feel the interaction succeeded, and presenting consistently regardless of audience.

Threat Scanning.fam: Clinical filing, internal only: Anxiety Disorders (canon.json's own R-tagged note, 'Filed as Anxiety Disorders'; translation-only per the HARD GUARD and CODE_ALIAS convention noted under Oscillation above). Note: canon.json's own filing names the broad category 'Anxiety Disorders,' not one specific disorder, and the record below is written at that same breadth rather than narrowed to a single diagnosis such as GAD.
Threat Scanning.def: A standing orientation toward detecting and preparing for possible threat, carried through persistent worry, active scanning of the environment for danger cues, and avoidance of situations that might contain the thing being scanned for.
Threat Scanning.body: Worrywart supplies persistent, hard-to-control anticipatory worry across situations. Hyper-Vigilant supplies active scanning of the environment for threat cues. Avoider supplies the behavioral response once a possible threat is flagged: staying away from the situation rather than testing whether the danger is real. The three together describe a closed loop -- worry generates scanning, scanning finds candidate threats, and avoidance prevents the loop from ever being tested against what actually happens.
Threat Scanning.inferenceBasis: The name, saboteur triad and clinical filing are owner-ruled (canon.json tag R). Unusually for this batch, each of the three saboteurs maps onto a separately, independently well-validated piece of the anxiety literature rather than one piece of literature split three ways -- see sourcing notes. The specific three-way packaging as a single named complex is still this project's own structural choice.
Threat Scanning.behavior: May worry persistently and across multiple topics even when nothing specific is wrong, notice and track potential danger cues in the environment that others do not register, and withdraw from or decline situations that could contain the thing being scanned for -- before any actual encounter tests whether the danger is present.
Threat Scanning.triggerMechanism: Ambiguous situations, novel environments, or any cue that could plausibly signal danger can activate the scanning response; once a candidate threat is flagged, avoidance follows quickly, which prevents the kind of direct experience that could update the original worry. This loop-closing structure is itself a well-documented feature of anxiety disorders, not unique to this record.
Threat Scanning.livedExample: Before a new social situation, the person generates several specific ways it could go wrong, monitors the room closely on arrival for any sign that one of those scenarios is unfolding, and leaves early or avoids the situation next time, without ever staying long enough to find out whether the feared outcome would actually have happened.
Threat Scanning.impact: Can narrow the person's range of situations, relationships and opportunities over time, since avoidance prevents the disconfirming experiences that would otherwise reduce the worry. Scanning can also be read by others as distrust or hostility, even when it is self-protective rather than accusatory.
Threat Scanning.practice: Name the specific feared outcome rather than staying with a general sense of unease. Test the prediction by staying in the situation rather than leaving early, when safety allows it. Track how often the scanned-for danger actually materializes versus how often it doesn't. Seek a qualified clinician if worry or avoidance is significantly limiting daily functioning -- exposure-based approaches are well-supported and this record is not a substitute for them.
Threat Scanning.oppositeDefinition: Calibrated assessment: noticing real signals of risk without continuous anticipatory worry, testing situations rather than avoiding them by default, and updating the assessment based on what actually happens.

Collapse.fam: Clinical filing, internal only: Depression (canon.json's own R-tagged note, 'Filed as Depression'; translation-only per the HARD GUARD and CODE_ALIAS convention noted under Oscillation above). NOTE: this name is also live, independently, as a hypercomplex-tier framework mode (Cluster III) -- see flag above, same issue as Rigidity.
Collapse.def: A contraction of agency in which a negative view of self and a settled expectation that nothing will improve combine with withdrawal from others, so that initiative narrows and disengagement starts to look like the only available response.
Collapse.body: Victim supplies the self-directed piece: sadness and a felt sense of being acted upon rather than acting, consistent with what Beck's cognitive model calls the self-pole of depressive thinking. Pessimist supplies the future-directed piece almost by name: a settled expectation that things will not get better, the core of what the hopelessness theory of depression describes directly. Loner supplies withdrawal from other people, which real research links bidirectionally to depression's course. Together they describe a pattern where little feels worth attempting and connection feels like it would not help even if attempted.
Collapse.inferenceBasis: The name, saboteur triad and clinical filing are owner-ruled (canon.json tag R). Unusually for this batch, the three saboteurs map onto three separately real and well-established bodies of work (Beck's cognitive triad, the hopelessness theory of depression, and the loneliness-depression literature) rather than one literature split three ways -- see sourcing notes. The specific three-way packaging as a single named complex, and its naming collision with the existing hypercomplex:Collapse record, are this project's own open questions, not resolved by the research below.
Collapse.behavior: May describe the self in persistently negative terms, expect that effort will not change the outcome and reduce or stop trying as a result, and pull back from social contact even when connection is available and previously welcomed. Initiative narrows: fewer things seem worth starting.
Collapse.triggerMechanism: A real setback, a pattern of setbacks, or an accumulation of unmet needs can activate the pattern; the hopelessness theory specifically proposes that stable, global causal attributions for a stressor ('this happened because of something permanent and pervasive about me or my situation') are what convert an ordinary setback into the hopelessness expectancy at the center of this complex, rather than the setback itself.
Collapse.livedExample: After a setback that has a specific, fixable cause, the person concludes that nothing they do will change their situation generally, stops reaching out to people who have previously been supportive, and describes the withdrawal as realistic rather than as a choice that is itself worsening the isolation.
Collapse.impact: Narrows problem-solving and access to support at exactly the point both would help most, since withdrawal removes the people and activities that could otherwise interrupt the pattern. Real research shows this loop runs in both directions: isolation deepens low mood, and low mood deepens isolation.
Collapse.practice: Reduce the task in front of you to one small, concrete, achievable next step rather than the whole situation. Separate a specific, fixable cause from a global conclusion about yourself or your prospects generally. Maintain at least minimal social contact even when it does not feel like it will help -- the research on withdrawal suggests the feeling is not a reliable guide here. Seek a qualified clinician if the pattern is severe or persistent; this record describes a working pattern, not a treatment plan, and must not be used to self-diagnose or diagnose someone else.
Collapse.oppositeDefinition: Supported engagement: taking small concrete actions even without certainty they will work, holding setbacks as specific rather than global, and maintaining connection to others as a resource rather than withdrawing from it.

Scatter.fam: Clinical filing, internal only: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (canon.json's own R-tagged note, 'Filed as ADHD'; translation-only per the HARD GUARD in SNIFFER_SPEC.md section 5 and section 11, and per engine.js/codes.js's CODE_ALIAS comment, 'a code is never shown as a diagnosis'). NOTE: unlike every other clinically-filed complex in canon.json's first 12 entries, this filing has no second internal source agreeing with it -- codes.js's own CODE_ALIAS row says plainly, 'the book's clinical list has no ADHD.' NOTE ALSO: CANON-MERGE-PLAN.md item D4 names Scatter as one of five owner-ruled complexes whose three saboteurs currently span more than one of the engine's internal saboteur 'families,' so compute() cannot produce this pairing from a live reading today; the document's own recommendation is to join the two systems, not to treat this as settled.
Scatter.def: A pattern of restless, energy-seeking movement toward stimulation, an attention that drifts toward internally generated thought rather than the task in front of a person, and a felt uncertainty about whether one's own account of oneself can be trusted, occurring together rather than as three separate traits.
Scatter.body: Restless supplies a pull toward activity and stimulation that resists sitting still or staying with one task. Dreamer supplies attention that detaches from the immediate task and drifts into internally generated thought. Imposter supplies a standing doubt about whether one's own functioning, account of events, or self-assessment can be trusted, even when there is real evidence to the contrary. Restless and Dreamer together describe much of what the DSM-5 names as the inattentive and hyperactive-impulsive presentations of ADHD; Imposter describes something adjacent but distinct, discussed below, that sits alongside rather than inside the DSM-5 criteria themselves.
Scatter.inferenceBasis: The name, glyph, saboteur triad and clinical filing are owner-ruled (canon.json tag R, 'Lance dictated' convention used elsewhere in this register for similar notes, though this specific shell's note does not use that exact phrase). The behavioral template below draws on real, named ADHD and mind-wandering literature for Restless and Dreamer specifically; the Imposter component is this project's own structural reading of the saboteur name, grounded only in thin, mostly non-peer-reviewed secondary material -- see sourcing notes, where I treat this the same way Batch 2 flagged its own weakest saboteur-to-criterion mapping (Imposter against BPD's identity disturbance) rather than presenting it with the same confidence as the Restless/Dreamer grounding.
Scatter.behavior: May seek activity, stimulation or movement and find sustained stillness genuinely difficult; attention may drift toward spontaneous, internally generated thought even during tasks that matter to the person, often without the person noticing the drift until it is pointed out; and the person may doubt their own account of their functioning, discounting real evidence of capability or progress as not representative of who they actually are.
Scatter.triggerMechanism: A task with low external stimulation, an unstructured gap, or an open-ended period can activate the pull toward movement or toward mind-wandering; a moment of real success or external validation can, separately, activate Imposter's doubt rather than settle it, because the standing doubt does not update symmetrically on positive and negative evidence. This is a working hypothesis about how the three saboteurs might co-occur, not a validated causal chain.
Scatter.livedExample: A person sits down to a task that requires sustained attention. Within minutes, attention has moved to an unrelated train of thought, noticed only once a deadline or another person's question interrupts it; the same person, told their work was good, responds with doubt about whether that assessment was accurate or whether they got away with something rather than actually having done well.
Scatter.impact: Can make task completion, time estimation and follow-through unpredictable from the outside, even when the person is capable of the work, because attention and energy are not reliably available on demand. The Imposter component can compound this by making the person's own account of their functioning an unreliable guide for others (and for themselves), since real competence is discounted rather than registered.
Scatter.practice: Build in movement or a stimulation outlet rather than fighting the pull toward it. Notice and name the drift of attention without judgment, and have a concrete way to return to the task. Separate the feeling of being a fraud from the actual evidence of one's own functioning, and write the evidence down rather than relying on the feeling to update itself. Seek a qualified clinical evaluation for ADHD if the pattern is persistent, present across settings, and functionally impairing -- this record describes a working pattern, not a diagnostic assessment, and must not be used to self-diagnose or diagnose someone else.
Scatter.oppositeDefinition: Directed engagement: sustaining attention and activity toward a chosen task with workable flexibility, and holding an accurate, evidence-based account of one's own functioning rather than a standing doubt that discounts real competence.

Anticipatory Freeze.fam: PID-5 / DSM-5 Alternative Model trait-domain placement, not an owner-dictated clinical filing: Negative Affectivity (canon.json's own I-tagged note, 'Negative Affectivity cluster. Anxiousness, perseveration and withdrawal co-load in PID-5.'). This is a dimensional trait domain, not a diagnosis; per the HARD GUARD in SNIFFER_SPEC.md sections 5 and 11, no score on this domain or this record is a diagnostic claim about any person.
Anticipatory Freeze.def: A pattern in which anticipating a demand or a possible negative outcome produces rumination on the anticipated problem, delay of the action itself, and withdrawal from the situation that would resolve the uncertainty -- motion stalls before it starts, rather than being attempted and failing.
Anticipatory Freeze.body: Overthinker supplies rumination that loops on a feared outcome rather than converging on a decision. Procrastinator supplies the delay of the action under that cloud of anticipated difficulty. Avoider supplies withdrawal from the situation itself once delay is no longer available. The three are sequential as much as simultaneous: thinking about the problem, then not starting it, then, if pressed, stepping away from it rather than through it. Canon's own note that these three 'co-load' in PID-5 reflects a real, documented pattern of cross-loading between Negative Affectivity's facets and adjacent domains, though I did not find a single study testing this exact three-facet grouping -- see sourcing notes.
Anticipatory Freeze.inferenceBasis: The name, saboteur triad and PID-5 framework placement are canon.json's own system-inferred entry (tag I), not Lance's direct dictation the way the R-tagged shells in Batches 1 and 2 were, and not my own invention either. The behavioral template below draws on three separately real literatures -- Negative Affectivity's factor structure, the procrastination literature, and the rumination/response-styles literature -- mapped onto this specific saboteur triad as a structural choice this project has not independently validated as a unified construct.
Anticipatory Freeze.behavior: May generate repeated, unresolved thinking about a feared outcome before acting; delay starting a task that carries anticipated difficulty, even past the point where delay has a cost; and withdraw from the situation entirely once direct avoidance becomes available, rather than attempting the task and risking the feared outcome directly.
Anticipatory Freeze.triggerMechanism: An upcoming demand, decision or evaluation with an uncertain or potentially negative outcome can activate rumination on the anticipated problem; as the deadline approaches without resolution, delay can give way to withdrawal from the situation altogether. This describes a possible sequence, not a fixed causal chain, and SNIFFER_SPEC.md's own note that Avoider 'fires in 81% of runs and costs 0.1 points' -- a saboteur the spec itself calls a weak signal because it fires almost always and changes almost nothing -- means this record's Avoider component should be read as a common, low-specificity endpoint rather than a strong diagnostic signal on its own.
Anticipatory Freeze.livedExample: A difficult conversation or task is anticipated days in advance. The person rehearses how it might go badly, repeatedly, without the rehearsal producing a plan; the task is pushed to the last possible moment; when the moment arrives, the person finds a reason the conversation or task cannot happen today either, and the underlying issue goes another cycle without resolution.
Anticipatory Freeze.impact: Can leave real decisions and tasks permanently deferred rather than completed or explicitly declined, since withdrawal removes the discomfort without resolving the underlying uncertainty. Other people may experience the pattern as unreliability rather than as anxiety, since the internal rumination is not visible from outside.
Anticipatory Freeze.practice: Name the specific feared outcome rather than staying with undirected rumination about it. Set a concrete, small first action with a fixed start time rather than waiting for the anticipated difficulty to resolve on its own. Notice the pull to withdraw as a signal to approach more slowly, not a signal to stop; test the actual outcome against the anticipated one rather than letting the anticipation stand unverified.
Anticipatory Freeze.oppositeDefinition: Approached uncertainty: naming an anticipated difficulty concretely, acting on a workable timeline despite not having resolved every unknown in advance, and testing a feared outcome against what actually happens rather than withdrawing before it can be tested.

Catastrophic Bracing.fam: PID-5 / DSM-5 Alternative Model trait-domain placement, not an owner-dictated clinical filing: Negative Affectivity, at its most intense pole (canon.json's own I-tagged note, 'Negative Affectivity at the high end. Fear 6 to 10 across all three profiles.'). A dimensional trait description, not a diagnosis; HARD GUARD applies as elsewhere in this document.
Catastrophic Bracing.def: A state of bracing for the worst possible outcome before it has happened or been confirmed -- catastrophic anticipation, persistent worry, and active scanning for danger cues combine so that the body and attention organize around an assumed worst case rather than the actual present situation.
Catastrophic Bracing.body: Catastrophizer supplies the leap to the worst possible interpretation of a given situation. Worrywart supplies sustained, hard-to-control worry that keeps the anticipated danger active. Hyper-Vigilant supplies continuous scanning of the environment for confirming threat cues. I checked canon's own claim that 'Fear 6 to 10' spans all three profiles directly against the registered saboteur bands: Catastrophizer's own fear band is 8-10, Worrywart's is 6-8, and Hyper-Vigilant's is 7-9 (confirmed in both registers.saboteurs and SNIFFER_SPEC.md section 3) -- so '6 to 10' is accurate as the combined span across the three profiles, not a claim that each individually reaches 6 and 10, and I confirmed that reading is correct rather than assuming it.
Catastrophic Bracing.inferenceBasis: The name, saboteur triad and PID-5 framework placement are canon.json's own system-inferred entry (tag I), not owner dictation and not my own invention. The behavioral template below draws on the Pain Catastrophizing Scale literature (generalized cautiously beyond its original pain-specific context), the well-replicated threat-attentional-bias literature, and the Fanselow predatory-imminence-continuum model as an illustrative parallel for canon's own 'the body already at the worst outcome' phrase; the specific three-saboteur packaging is this project's structural choice, not an independently validated unified construct.
Catastrophic Bracing.behavior: May interpret an ambiguous or uncertain situation as already heading toward the worst plausible outcome, hold that anticipated outcome in mind persistently rather than letting it resolve, and actively scan the immediate environment for cues that would confirm the feared outcome is arriving -- the three operating together rather than in sequence, so the body can be in a state of bracing well before any actual danger has appeared.
Catastrophic Bracing.triggerMechanism: An ambiguous cue, a situation with an uncertain outcome, or a reminder of a past bad outcome can activate the catastrophic leap; once active, worry sustains the anticipated threat and vigilance keeps searching the environment for confirmation, which can create a self-sustaining loop largely independent of what is actually happening. Fanselow's predatory-imminence model offers a useful parallel here -- as perceived imminence of a threat increases, defensive behavior shifts from anxious anticipation toward panic-like bracing -- but this is offered as an illustrative frame from a different literature, not a direct finding about this named complex.
Catastrophic Bracing.livedExample: A minor physical symptom appears. Before any medical information is available, the person has already moved mentally to the most severe possible explanation, cannot stop returning to that explanation over the following hours, and begins noticing and tracking every subsequent sensation as possible further confirmation of it.
Catastrophic Bracing.impact: Can produce a body and attention that are chronically braced for danger that has not actually arrived, which is exhausting on its own terms and can also prompt decisions (avoidance, repeated reassurance-seeking, premature worst-case action) based on the anticipated outcome rather than the actual one.
Catastrophic Bracing.practice: Separate the worst-case interpretation from the most likely interpretation, and name both explicitly rather than letting the worst case stand unexamined. Track how often the anticipated worst outcome actually occurs, as a direct check on the catastrophizing pattern. Reduce active scanning deliberately when no new information has arrived, since continued scanning without new information sustains the bracing rather than resolving it. Seek a qualified clinician if the pattern is severe, persistent or physically exhausting.
Catastrophic Bracing.oppositeDefinition: Calibrated readiness: assessing a situation's actual likely range of outcomes, holding worry proportionate to real risk, and scanning for genuine new information rather than continuously re-confirming an assumed worst case.

Meaning Withdrawal.fam: PID-5 / DSM-5 Alternative Model trait-domain placement, not an owner-dictated clinical filing: Detachment (canon.json's own I-tagged note, 'Detachment spectrum. Anhedonia plus restricted affectivity.'). A dimensional trait description, not a diagnosis; HARD GUARD applies as elsewhere in this document. NOTE: the shell's own characterization, 'all three are disgust-plus-sadness profiles,' is accurate for Nihilist and Cynic but not for Pessimist, whose registered bands (confirmed in both registers.saboteurs and SNIFFER_SPEC.md section 3) are sadness and fear, not disgust -- see flag above.
Meaning Withdrawal.def: A withdrawal of felt meaning and expected reward from experience: a global sense that nothing is worth much (nihilism), a defended distrust that keeps people and effort at a distance (cynicism), and an expectation that things will not improve (pessimism), together producing reduced engagement rather than active distress.
Meaning Withdrawal.body: Nihilist supplies a global devaluing of meaning or worth across situations, not limited to one disappointment. Cynic supplies a defended distrust that treats sincerity, effort or other people's motives with suspicion, functioning partly as self-protection against further disappointment. Pessimist supplies an expectation that outcomes will not improve, running more on sadness and fear of a bad outcome than on disgust. Together they describe a flattened, low-reward relationship to experience that sits closer to withdrawal than to acute distress -- the PID-5 Detachment domain's territory, specifically its anhedonia and restricted-affectivity facets, rather than Negative Affectivity's more acutely distressed territory.
Meaning Withdrawal.inferenceBasis: The name, saboteur triad and PID-5 framework placement are canon.json's own system-inferred entry (tag I), not owner dictation and not my own invention. The behavioral template below draws on Frankl's existential-vacuum concept (named but clinical-philosophical rather than quantitatively empirical), the Maslach Burnout Inventory's and Cook-Medley Hostility Scale's real, separate cynicism research, and DSM-5's anhedonia criterion plus the PID-5 Detachment domain's facet structure; the specific three-saboteur packaging is this project's structural choice, not an independently validated unified construct, and the shell's own 'disgust-plus-sadness' description does not hold for all three members, as noted above.
Meaning Withdrawal.behavior: May describe activities, goals or relationships as not really worth the effort, independent of how they are actually going; may treat other people's stated motives, warmth or sincerity with habitual suspicion, keeping a guarded distance as a default rather than a response to a specific breach of trust; and may expect that a given situation will not improve, reducing effort toward it in advance of any actual evidence that effort would fail.
Meaning Withdrawal.triggerMechanism: An accumulation of disappointments, a loss of a previously organizing goal or belief, or repeated experiences of others' stated motives not matching their actions can activate withdrawal of meaning, distrust, or lowered expectation respectively; once active, each can reinforce the others, since devalued meaning reduces the motivation to test distrust or pessimism against new evidence.
Meaning Withdrawal.livedExample: A person who previously invested real effort in a goal, relationship or cause stops describing it as mattering, responds to a colleague's or partner's supportive gesture with suspicion about what it is really for, and predicts in advance that an upcoming opportunity will not amount to anything -- then puts in correspondingly less effort, which tends to confirm the prediction.
Meaning Withdrawal.impact: Can produce a self-sustaining low-engagement state: reduced meaning lowers motivation, lowered motivation reduces effort, and reduced effort produces the disappointing outcomes that confirm the original devaluation, distrust or pessimism. Relationships can read the pattern as indifference rather than as a defended response to past disappointment.
Meaning Withdrawal.practice: Name one specific area where meaning, trust or expectation has narrowed, rather than treating the devaluation as global and permanent. Test a specific prediction of failure or a specific suspicion against actual evidence rather than letting it stand unverified. Reintroduce small, low-stakes engagement in one area as a direct test of whether the expected lack of reward actually holds. Seek a qualified clinician if the pattern is pervasive, persistent or affecting functioning -- this record describes a working pattern, not a treatment plan.
Meaning Withdrawal.oppositeDefinition: Re-engaged valuation: recognizing specific sources of meaning and reward without requiring global certainty, extending provisional trust that updates on actual evidence, and testing expectations of outcome against what actually happens rather than withdrawing effort in advance.

Retreat.fam: PID-5 / DSM-5 Alternative Model trait-domain placement, not an owner-dictated clinical filing: Detachment (canon.json's own I-tagged note, 'Detachment. Withdrawal and intimacy avoidance.'). A dimensional trait description, not a diagnosis; HARD GUARD applies as elsewhere in this document. This territory also overlaps with HiTOP's own, separate Detachment spectrum (schizoid, avoidant and dependent personality pathology), a related but distinct framework from the PID-5 domain of the same name -- see sourcing notes.
Retreat.def: Leaving an unwanted present situation without necessarily leaving the room: through physical and emotional distance from other people, through a restriction of interest in closeness itself, or through attention and energy redirected into imagined alternatives rather than the present situation.
Retreat.body: Loner supplies a preference for distance from other people and restricted interest in closeness itself, rather than distance driven by fear of others. Escapist supplies withdrawal from an unwanted situation through absorption in an alternative activity (classically media, gaming, or fantasy) rather than direct confrontation or negotiation of the situation. Dreamer supplies attention and energy redirected into imagined alternatives, which can function as a form of leaving without physically leaving. Canon's own phrase, 'leaving the room, by distance or by fantasy,' names exactly this: two routes (literal/relational distance, and imaginative absorption) to the same underlying exit.
Retreat.inferenceBasis: The name, saboteur triad and PID-5/Detachment framework placement are canon.json's own system-inferred entry (tag I), not owner dictation and not my own invention. The behavioral template below draws on DSM-5 schizoid personality disorder criteria, the HiTOP Detachment spectrum, Bartholomew & Horowitz's dismissing-avoidant attachment style, and Kardefelt-Winther's compensatory internet-use model; the specific three-saboteur packaging, and the extension of escapism research (studied mainly in gaming/media contexts) to a broader 'leaving by fantasy' framing, are this project's own structural choices.
Retreat.behavior: May prefer solitary activity and show limited interest in close relationships, not out of fear of other people but because closeness itself is not strongly sought; may withdraw into an absorbing alternative activity when a present situation becomes unwanted, rather than engaging with or exiting the situation directly; and may spend substantial attention on imagined alternatives to the present circumstance.
Retreat.triggerMechanism: An unwanted social demand, conflict, or situation experienced as depleting or stressful can activate a shift toward solitary activity, toward an absorbing alternative activity, or toward imaginative absorption, functioning as a substitute for directly engaging with or resolving the triggering situation.
Retreat.livedExample: A gathering or obligation that the person finds draining is attended physically but not really joined -- the person finds a reason to step away, or stays present but visibly absorbed in a phone, a private train of thought, or an imagined different circumstance, rather than engaging with the people in the room or leaving outright.
Retreat.impact: Can leave real relational needs and unresolved situations unaddressed, since the exit (physical distance, absorbing activity, or fantasy) relieves the immediate discomfort without requiring the underlying situation to be engaged or resolved. Other people may read the pattern as disinterest rather than as a coping response to an unwanted demand.
Retreat.practice: Name the specific situation being exited, rather than treating the pull to withdraw as undirected. Distinguish wanting less closeness as a genuine preference from using distance, absorption or fantasy to avoid a specific unresolved conflict or demand. Where an alternative activity (media, fantasy, solitary pursuits) functions as the primary coping response to stress, test a direct, low-stakes engagement with the avoided situation as an alternative to withdrawing from it.
Retreat.oppositeDefinition: Present engagement: remaining available to people and situations that are unwanted or difficult long enough to address them directly, using solitude or imagination as a genuine preference or a deliberate rest rather than as the default exit from discomfort.

Cold Analysis.fam: PID-5 / DSM-5 Alternative Model trait-domain placement, not an owner-dictated clinical filing: Detachment crossing into Antagonism (canon.json's own I-tagged note). A dimensional trait description, not a diagnosis; HARD GUARD applies as elsewhere in this document. NOTE, the central flag of this record: canon.json's own registers.hyper_complexes[1] ('Sociopathy') already names Cold Analysis, alongside Narcissistic, as 'the empathy-off cluster' of that hyper-complex, which SNIFFER_SPEC.md section 5's own descent chain (Narcissism -> Machiavellianism -> Sociopathy -> Psychopathy -> Megalomania) places one rung below the existing, deep descent:Psychopathy record in engine.js. Cold Analysis.def: A stance that processes situations and other people primarily through detached, logical analysis, with emotional responsiveness and interpersonal warmth reduced to the point that moral or critical judgment of others can proceed without the ordinary felt check that another person's distress usually provides.
Cold Analysis.body: Hyper-Rational supplies a default mode of detached, logic-first processing in which emotional information is discounted or absent. Skeptic supplies a standing distrust of others' stated motives and claims. Judge supplies moral or critical evaluation of other people. Where Dominance Enforcement (Batch 1) paired Judge with Controller's active management of outcomes, and Machiavellian Tactics (Batch 1) paired Skeptic with Manipulator's active deception, this complex pairs both with Hyper-Rational instead, so the resulting judgment and distrust proceed with the emotional responsiveness that would normally accompany them substantially reduced -- canon's own phrase, 'judgement with the feeling switched off,' names this precisely.
Cold Analysis.inferenceBasis: The name, saboteur triad and PID-5/Detachment-crossing-Antagonism framework placement are canon.json's own system-inferred entry (tag I), not owner dictation and not my own invention. The behavioral template below draws on PID-5's Antagonism-domain callousness facet, the Detachment domain's restricted-affectivity facet, alexithymia research, and the callous-unemotional-traits literature from developmental psychopathology research; the specific three-saboteur packaging is this project's structural choice. Separately and importantly: this record's conceptual link to descent:Psychopathy, via canon.json's own Sociopathy hyper-complex, is not this project's inference -- it is already asserted in canon.json today (tag I), and is flagged above rather than treated as resolved or as a basis for this record's confidence score.
Cold Analysis.behavior: May process a difficult or emotionally loaded situation primarily through logical analysis, with little visible emotional response even where one would ordinarily be expected; may treat others' stated motives, explanations or distress claims with routine suspicion rather than taking them at face value; and may render moral or critical judgment on another person's conduct without the ordinary felt hesitation that comes from registering the impact of that judgment on the other person.
Cold Analysis.triggerMechanism: A situation calling for an emotional response, a claim or explanation from another person, or an opportunity to evaluate someone else's conduct can activate a default shift toward detached analysis, suspicion of the other party's account, and judgment delivered without the usual emotional moderation. This describes a possible processing style, not a validated causal mechanism, and must not be used to infer psychopathy, sociopathy or any clinical construct from a single instance of cool or critical behavior.
Cold Analysis.livedExample: A colleague explains a personal difficulty that affected their work. The response is a dispassionate analysis of the work's shortfalls and what should change, delivered without acknowledgment of the colleague's stated difficulty and without visible discomfort at delivering a critical assessment in that context.
Cold Analysis.impact: Can leave other people feeling unseen or judged without recourse, since the ordinary emotional signals that would normally soften or contextualize a critical judgment are reduced or absent. Decisions made this way may be internally consistent and well-reasoned while still causing real relational harm that the person making them does not register as a cost worth weighing.
Cold Analysis.practice: Before rendering judgment, name explicitly what the other person's account or distress actually is, separate from the logical analysis of the situation. Check deliberately for the emotional impact of a planned judgment on the other person, since it may not register automatically. Treat suspicion of another person's motives as a hypothesis to test against evidence, not a default starting assumption. Where the pattern is severe, pervasive, or associated with disregard for others' welfare, this moves into territory that needs a qualified clinician alongside, not a self-directed practice -- consistent with how engine.js's own descent:Psychopathy record already instructs.
Cold Analysis.oppositeDefinition: Warm discernment: analyzing a situation clearly and critically while registering and weighing its emotional impact on the people involved, extending provisional trust rather than default suspicion, and delivering judgment, when warranted, with the feeling intact rather than switched off.

Self-Erasure.fam: Schema-therapy domain placement, not an owner-dictated clinical filing: Other- Directedness (canon.json's own I-tagged note). A trait/schema description, not a diagnosis -- no DSM category is named here, and none should be read into it. NOTE: a 2018 peer-reviewed reclassification (Bach, Lockwood & Young) moves one of the shell's three component schemas, Self-Sacrifice, to a different domain than the one the shell names; see flag above.
Self-Erasure.def: Handing control of one's own choices to another person, suppressing one's own wants to avoid conflict or disapproval, and pursuing approval at the cost of a stable, separate sense of self -- three related moves that together trade the self for the relationship meant to hold it.
Self-Erasure.body: Pleaser supplies the drive toward acceptance and away from disapproval that organizes behavior around what will be approved of rather than what is wanted. People-Pleaser supplies the more literal behavioral layer: agreeing, accommodating, and suppressing disagreement to keep the relationship warm. Enabler supplies a further move past accommodation: absorbing or smoothing over another person's problematic behavior rather than naming it, so the bond is protected even at the cost of letting a real problem continue. None of the three saboteurs here span more than one of engine.js's internal saboteur families (all three code to the same family, Collapse), so unlike two of the other four records in this batch, this one is not blocked from a live reading by that specific mechanism.
Self-Erasure.inferenceBasis: The name, saboteur triad and schema-domain placement are canon.json's own system-inferred entry (tag I), not owner dictation and not my own invention. The behavioral template below draws on Young's real, named Other-Directedness domain for Pleaser and People-Pleaser's shared contribution; Enabler's contribution draws on a real but genuinely contested academic literature (codependency/enabling has no DSM or ICD entry and no settled definition -- see sourcing notes), which is why this record's confidence sits lower than Sacrificial Ledger's, its closest sibling in this batch.
Self-Erasure.behavior: May defer decisions that affect their own life to another person's preference rather than state and hold their own, suppress disagreement or a competing want specifically to avoid the other person's displeasure, and smooth over, excuse or absorb the practical consequences of another person's harmful or irresponsible behavior rather than name it as a problem.
Self-Erasure.triggerMechanism: A cue that disagreement or an expressed want could cost approval or provoke conflict can activate suppression of that want before it is ever stated. Separately, a partner or family member's harmful behavior becoming visible can activate absorbing its consequences instead of naming the behavior, when naming it risks the relationship itself.
Self-Erasure.livedExample: Asked what they want to do, the person first tries to infer what the other person wants and offers that instead, presenting it as their own preference. When the other person's behavior later causes a real problem, the person manages the fallout quietly rather than raising the behavior that caused it, and describes this afterward as keeping the peace.
Self-Erasure.impact: The person's own preferences become unreliable information to the people around them, because what is stated is shaped by what will be approved of rather than what is actually wanted. Problems that need to be named to be addressed instead get absorbed, so they tend to recur, and the person's own sense of self narrows to whatever role keeps the bond intact.
Self-Erasure.practice: Before answering what you want, notice whether the answer is forming around what will be approved of. State an actual preference even when it might not be welcomed, starting with low-stakes choices. Before absorbing a consequence of someone else's behavior, name the behavior itself, separately from whether the relationship can survive the naming.
Self-Erasure.oppositeDefinition: Standing presence: holding and stating one's own preferences and limits even when they might not be approved of, and naming a problem in another person's behavior rather than absorbing its consequences to protect the bond.
